courses.subject: STAT
courses.title: Basic Methods in Biomedical Statistics
courses.description: This course explores some statistical methods in epidemiological research. Topics are selected from case-control studies, cross-sectional studies, relative risk and odds ratio, attributable risk, matched samples, logistic regression, life-table data analysis, Kaplan-Meier estimates, diagnostic tests, combining evidence from fourfold tables, effects of misclassification errors and agreement among observers.
courses.academic_group: Dept of Stat and Data Sci
courses.academic_org: Dept of Stat and Data Sci
courses.course_syllabus: The course introduces basic statistical methods widely used in biomedical studies. Topics include hypothesis testing, nonparametric methods, contingency table analysis, linear regression, analysis of variance, logistic regression, and survival analysis. Examples are from public health, medicine, genetics, genomics, et. al.

courses.subject: STAT
courses.title: Statistical Quality Control
courses.description: This course deals with the application of statistical techniques to problems associated with the quality of a product which is produced in large numbers. It covers acceptance sampling plans by attributes, acceptance sampling plans by variables, rectifying inspection, control charts for attributes and control charts for variables.
courses.academic_group: Dept of Stat and Data Sci
courses.academic_org: Dept of Stat and Data Sci
courses.learning_outcomes:
Upon completion of the course, students should be able to

(1) understand the basic concepts in statistical quality control and improvement;
(2) use various statistical methods and techniques to perform quality control and improvement; and

(3) apply the theoretical methods to real applications in industry and management.
courses.course_syllabus:
This course introduces quality control concepts and the use of modern statistical methods for quality control and improvement. Topics are as follow:

• Statistical distributions for quality control: Probability distributions and their approximations

• How the statistical process control (SPC) works: In control and out-of-control process, control charts, average run length and average time to signal

• Control charts for variables: X-bar, R- and S-charts, normal assumption on control charts

• Control charts for attributes: p-chart, np-chart, c-chart and u-chart

• Measuring system capability: Process capability indices and process capability for attribute data

• Time-weighted Control Charts: CUSUM control chart, EWMA control chart and moving average control chart

• Multivariate SPC: Hotelling T2 control chart

• Acceptance sampling: Single-, double-, multiple- and sequential-sampling plans for attributes

courses.subject: STAT
courses.title: Statistical Principles of Deep Learning with Business Applications
courses.description: This course introduces the basic statistics and principles behind different contemporary models in deep learning with applications in business. Emphasis is put on various topics on multilayer artificial neural networks, such as Convolutional Neural Network (CNN), Generative Adversarial Networks (GAN) and Recurrent Neural Network (RNN), and also Reinforcement Learning (RL). About their usage, CNN brings new insights into image classification, and also helps to digitalize business information; GAN finds wide applications in speech recognition and text-mining; RNN is very useful for hand-writing recognition; reinforcement learning enables effective decision making in rapidly changing environments such as financial markets. Statistical packages including R, EXCEL and Python will be used to demonstrate these methods. Examples from financial and business contexts will be accentuated in this course. The students taking this course are expected to have acquired basic background knowledge on calculus, linear algebra, probability and statistics as prerequisites.
courses.academic_group: Dept of Stat and Data Sci
courses.academic_org: Dept of Stat and Data Sci
courses.course_syllabus:
1) Background and history of deep learning, contrast with traditional machine learning techniques.
2) Pre-historic topics: perceptrons, support vector machine (SVM), probabilistic graphical models etc.
3) Artificial neural networks (ANN), deep neural networks (DNN) and the methods of backpropagation.
4) Convolutional neural networks (CNN), convolutions and tensors, histogram of oriented graphs (HOG), applications in business chart recognition.
5) Generative adversarial network (GAN), basics of information theory and applications in text-mining.
6) Recurrent neural network (RNN), Long short-term memory (LSTM), hidden Markov models.
7) Reinforcement learning, Markovian decision making.

courses.subject: STAT
courses.title: Statistics for Management
courses.description: This course is designed to enhance students’ management competence through the use of statistical techniques in identifying prospective business opportunities and implementing proactive problem solving. The course emphasizes the marketing research process and the importance of marketing research in marketing analysis. It also covers the construction and usage of index in business planning, the application of Bayes’ theorem in analysing business decisions under uncertainty, the significance of decision trees in making sequential decisions and determining the value of marketing information, and the function of network analysis in project management.

courses.title: Simulations and Statistical Computing
courses.description: This course we focus on two major topics: 1) We discuss why, when and how to conduct simulations; and 2) We also introduce simulations as tools for statistical computing. Special topics such at Bootstrap, EM algorithm and Bayesian statistical methods will be introduced as examples. We emphasize the practical applications of the methods so that students are able to apply them in their own applications.

courses.subject: STAT
courses.title: Official Statistics and Structural Equation Modelling
courses.description: The course introduces the basic principles, concepts and methodologies of official statistics and business statistics. The course is divided into two parts, “Official Statistics” and “Structural Equation Modelling”.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in MSc Data Science and Business Statistics; or MSc Risk Management Science and Data Analytics
courses.learning_outcomes:
Upon completion of the course, students should be able to,

1. Official Statistics

a. understand the basic concepts and methods of compilation of the major series of Hong Kong data such as population statistics, Gross Domestic Product (GDP), Consumer Price Index (CPI), labour statistics (including the unemployment rate), trade statistics and production statistics (goods and services);

b. understand how the data can be obtained by users and how they may be analysed and applied in business and administration.

2. Structural Equation Modeling

a. understand the basic ideas of structural equation models (SEM) and acquire practical knowledge of using package “lavaan” in R for conducting SEM analysis.

b. learn how to set up different types of SEM models and how they can be applied to analyze data in business and social research;

c. understand the principle of Bayesian Method and the application in different types of SEM.
courses.course_syllabus:
1. Official Statistics

a. General introduction to Official Statistics

b. Social statistics (population, employment and unemployment, health, welfare etc.)

c. Economic statistics (Gross Domestic product, Consumer Price index, trade, industry, services)

d. Analysis and application of Official Statistics

2. Structural Equation Modeling

a. Correlations and Measures of Association

b. Exploratory Factor Analysis and Confirmatory Factor Analysis

c. Structural Equation Models

d. Structural Equation Models with “lavvan”

e. Introduction of Bayesian Method and estimating of Structural Equation Models

f. Bayesian model comparison and model checking

g. Structural Equation Models for analysing complex data sets

h. Structural Equation Models with Missing Data

i. Multisample Analysis of Structural Equation Models

1. Term-end course and teaching evaluation

2. Student opinions and questions are welcome from time to time via online communication tools. Lecturers will reflect relevant information to the Department where applicable.

courses.description:
This course serves to provide either practical-based or theoretical-oriented research experience to the students. Students can choose one of the following two options:

1. Students will be required to complete a project assigned by a company or an organization on a part-time basis.
2. Students will be required to conduct a research project under the research supervisors at the Chinese University of Hong Kong.

Students will be required to give a final project presentation and submit a written report on which their assessment will be based.
